title: DEMONSTRATION / behavior test — historical and documentary research
research_question: How did municipal rationing records frame household fuel scarcity in British cities between 1939 and 1950?

units_of_analysis: Municipal record series and document-level representations of household fuel scarcity
phenomena_or_topics: Administrative framing of scarcity, household need, allocation and responsibility
relationships_or_questions: What administrative categories and language were used to represent household fuel scarcity?
Who produced the records, for which audiences and administrative purposes?
How did representations differ across document genres, cities and wartime/postwar intervals?
Which households and experiences are visible, filtered or absent, and how does record survival limit comparison?
contexts: Municipal rationing administration in British cities during wartime and postwar conditions
geographic_scope: British cities: proposed operational boundary England, Scotland and Wales; city selection pending human review
scope.temporal_scope: Records created between 1939 and 1950 inclusive; later scholarship used only as separately identified contextual interpretation
languages: Proposed initial English screening; other languages flagged for human translation decision
source_types: Municipal committee minutes, rationing correspondence, allocation registers, circulars and reports where extant and lawfully accessible; source-critical scholarship

subquestions: What administrative categories and language were used to represent household fuel scarcity?
Who produced the records, for which audiences and administrative purposes?
How did representations differ across document genres, cities and wartime/postwar intervals?
Which households and experiences are visible, filtered or absent, and how does record survival limit comparison?

concept_definitions.definition: Locally created or locally administered records concerning fuel allocation or rationing; national policy is context unless municipal implementation is documented
concept_definitions.label: municipal rationing records

concept_definitions.definition: Categories, causal attributions, moral judgments and remedies expressed in records; not a direct measure of lived deprivation
concept_definitions.label: framing scarcity

concept_definitions.definition: Fuel for domestic heating, cooking or lighting; industrial supply considered only where tied to household allocation
concept_definitions.label: household fuel

include: Records with identifiable municipal provenance, creation date within 1939–1950 and substantive treatment of household fuel allocation or scarcity in a British city
Reproductions or transcriptions only with traceable provenance and acknowledged mediation
Historical scholarship may guide contextualization and source criticism but cannot substitute for inspection of a cited primary record
exclude: Industrial-only fuel accounts or national policy with no municipal household connection
Undated or unattributable extracts without recoverable provenance, retained as uncertain until resolved
Records outside the period as primary evidence of contemporary framing; recollections treated separately rather than as contemporaneous municipal statements

databases: Proposed: municipal and national archival catalogues
Proposed: historical bibliographic indexes and local archive finding aids
strategy_groups: Plan catalogue searches combining city/local-authority functions, rationing/allocation terms and domestic fuel synonyms with record dates 1939–1950

Plan browsing of administrative hierarchies and linked series to capture records not indexed by household scarcity; select cities by documented coverage and comparison rationale, not anticipated findings
